name: Galileo Galilei
note: A room of what Galileo actually published, in translations that are genuinely out of copyright. The two works Project Gutenberg holds are here in full; Two New Sciences is transcribed from the 1914 Crew and de Salvio translation, split into its four Days as Galileo wrote it, with the page scan linked alongside for the diagrams. The Letter to the Grand Duchess Christina is deliberately absent — the translation everyone quotes is Stillman Drake's from 1957 and is still in copyright. The public-domain alternative is Thomas Salusbury's of 1661, in his Mathematical Collections and Translations; when a clean scan of that is prepared the letter belongs here, and it is the most important thing missing.

works.title: The Sidereal Messenger (Sidereus Nuncius, Venice, 1610)
works.source: tr. Edward Stafford Carlos, 1880 · Project Gutenberg #46036 · public domain
works.note: Written in weeks and printed in a hurry: mountains on the moon, the Milky Way resolved into stars, and four bodies moving around Jupiter that he named for the Medici. The book that made him famous and made the trouble.

works.title: Discourse Concerning the Natation of Bodies Upon, and Submersion In, the Water (1612)
works.source: tr. Thomas Salusbury, 1663 · Project Gutenberg #37729 · public domain
works.note: Presented to Cosimo II. An argument with the Aristotelians about why things float — shape or density — and an early demonstration of what he meant by settling a question with an experiment rather than an authority. Salusbury's seventeenth-century English is kept as printed.

works.title: Dialogues Concerning Two New Sciences (Leiden, 1638) — On the Resistance of Solids
works.source: tr. Henry Crew and Alfonso de Salvio, Macmillan, 1914 · Internet Archive, Cornell copy · public domain
works.note: The workmen in the Venetian arsenal, and from that opening scene the question of why a large ship or a large bone cannot simply be a small one scaled up. Also the vacuum, the speed of light, and the pendulum. Written blind and under house arrest at Arcetri, smuggled out to a Dutch printer because he was forbidden to publish. Transcribed from the 1914 scan; a handful of OCR ligature errors have been corrected.

works.title: Dialogues Concerning Two New Sciences (Leiden, 1638) — On the Strength of Beams
works.source: tr. Henry Crew and Alfonso de Salvio, Macmillan, 1914 · Internet Archive, Cornell copy · public domain
works.note: The mathematics of breaking: where a loaded beam gives way, and why. The section Newton and every engineer after him inherited. Written blind and under house arrest at Arcetri, smuggled out to a Dutch printer because he was forbidden to publish. Transcribed from the 1914 scan; a handful of OCR ligature errors have been corrected.

works.title: Dialogues Concerning Two New Sciences (Leiden, 1638) — On Naturally Accelerated Motion
works.source: tr. Henry Crew and Alfonso de Salvio, Macmillan, 1914 · Internet Archive, Cornell copy · public domain
works.note: The law of falling bodies, set out as a new science of an ancient subject. Distances as the squares of the times, demonstrated on an inclined plane. Written blind and under house arrest at Arcetri, smuggled out to a Dutch printer because he was forbidden to publish. Transcribed from the 1914 scan; a handful of OCR ligature errors have been corrected.

works.title: Dialogues Concerning Two New Sciences (Leiden, 1638) — On the Motion of Projectiles
works.source: tr. Henry Crew and Alfonso de Salvio, Macmillan, 1914 · Internet Archive, Cornell copy · public domain
works.note: That a projectile traces a parabola: uniform motion horizontally, accelerated motion downward, combined. The last thing he published. Written blind and under house arrest at Arcetri, smuggled out to a Dutch printer because he was forbidden to publish. Transcribed from the 1914 scan; a handful of OCR ligature errors have been corrected.
